title: Nigeria's NGX Stock Rally: Up 62% in 2026, Driven by Local Investors | The Six, Ep. 14
lede: Nigeria's NGX All-Share Index has gained 62% this year to Nov. 13, and listed shares are worth almost ₦164 trillion, up from ₦99 trillion in January. Behind the rally: a steadier naira, falling inflation, the largest rate cut since 2006 and a bank recapitalisation drive. But foreign investors have been net sellers, and Nigerians now account for about nine in ten naira traded.
keyPoints: The NGX All-Share Index closed at 252,269.16 on Nov. 13, 2026, up 62.11% year to date from 155,613.03; equity market capitalisation reached ₦163.80 trillion, up from ₦99.38 trillion at the start of the year (Nairametrics; ThisDay).

The naira, floated in June 2023 when the Central Bank of Nigeria unified exchange rates, ended 2025 at ₦1,429 per dollar, its first annual gain in 13 years, and closed at ₦1,358.50 on Nov. 12, 2026 (AP; Nairametrics).

Inflation eased to 14.63% in September 2026, and the CBN cut its policy rate by 350 basis points to 23%, its largest cut since 2006. By March 6, 2026, 30 of 33 banks had met new minimum capital requirements (NBS; CBN via Premium Times).

Foreign investors made up 10.26% of NGX trading in January–September 2026, down from 21.56% a year earlier, with outflows of ₦913.61 billion against inflows of ₦632.35 billion. Domestic trading doubled to ₦13.52 trillion (NGX Domestic and Foreign Portfolio Investment Report via ThisDay).
Eleven blue-chip companies held 75.9% of the market's value on Oct. 30; Dangote Cement (₦23.96 trillion) and Airtel Africa (₦23.68 trillion) lead (ThisDay via allAfrica).
